chrome.name: ERR_IO_PENDING
chrome.desc: An asynchronous IO operation is not yet complete. This usually does not indicate a fatal error. Typically this error will be generated as a notification to wait for some external notification that the IO operation finally completed.

chrome.name: ERR_FAILED
chrome.desc: A generic failure occurred.

chrome.name: ERR_ABORTED
chrome.desc: An operation was aborted (due to user action).

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
chrome.desc: An argument to the function is incorrect.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_HANDLE
chrome.desc: The handle or file descriptor is invalid.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND
chrome.desc: The file or directory cannot be found.

chrome.name: ERR_TIMED_OUT
chrome.desc: An operation timed out.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_TOO_BIG
chrome.desc: The file is too large.

chrome.name: ERR_UNEXPECTED
chrome.desc: An unexpected error. This may be caused by a programming mistake or an invalid assumption.

chrome.name: ERR_ACCESS_DENIED
chrome.desc: Permission to access a resource, other than the network, was denied.

chrome.name: ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
chrome.desc: The operation failed because of unimplemented functionality.

chrome.name: ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES
chrome.desc: There were not enough resources to complete the operation.

chrome.name: ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
chrome.desc: Memory allocation failed.

chrome.name: ERR_UPLOAD_FILE_CHANGED
chrome.desc: The file upload failed because the file's modification time was different from the expectation.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_NOT_CONNECTED
chrome.desc: The socket is not connected.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_EXISTS
chrome.desc: The file already exists.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_PATH_TOO_LONG
chrome.desc: The path or file name is too long.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_NO_SPACE
chrome.desc: Not enough room left on the disk.

chrome.name: ERR_FILE_VIRUS_INFECTED
chrome.desc: The file has a virus.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
chrome.desc: The client chose to block the request.

chrome.name: ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED
chrome.desc: The network changed.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by the URL block list configured by the domain administrator.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_IS_CONNECTED
chrome.desc: The socket is already connected.

chrome.name: ERR_UPLOAD_STREAM_REWIND_NOT_SUPPORTED
chrome.desc: The upload failed because the upload stream needed to be re-read, due to a retry or a redirect, but the upload stream doesn't support that operation.

chrome.name: ERR_CONTEXT_SHUT_DOWN
chrome.desc: The request failed because the URLRequestContext is shutting down, or has been shut down.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE
chrome.desc: The request failed because the response was delivered along with requirements which are not met ('X-Frame-Options' and 'Content-Security-Policy' ancestor checks and 'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy' for instance).

chrome.name: ERR_CLEARTEXT_NOT_PERMITTED
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by system policy disallowing some or all cleartext requests. Used for NetworkSecurityPolicy on Android.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by a Content Security Policy

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by CORB or ORB.

chrome.name: ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_REVOKED
chrome.desc: The request was blocked because it originated from a frame that has disabled network access.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_BY_FINGERPRINTING_PROTECTION
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by fingerprinting protections.

chrome.name: ERR_BLOCKED_IN_INCOGNITO_BY_ADMINISTRATOR
chrome.desc: The request was blocked by the Incognito Mode URL block list configured by the domain administrator.

chrome.name: ERR_LOCAL_NETWORK_PERMISSION_MISSING
chrome.desc: The request was blocked because the local network permission is missing. Note that this is different from BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS which is specifically for a CORS error code.

chrome.name: ERR_STRICT_ECH_REQUIRED
chrome.desc: The request was blocked because ECH is strictly required, but: - The client could not obtain a valid ECH configuration. - The server rejected the ECH, and the client failed to establish a new ECH connection after retrying with retry_configs.

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED
chrome.desc: A connection was closed (corresponding to a TCP FIN).

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_RESET
chrome.desc: A connection was reset (corresponding to a TCP RST).

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
chrome.desc: A connection attempt was refused.

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED
chrome.desc: A connection timed out as a result of not receiving an ACK for data sent. This can include a FIN packet that did not get ACK'd.

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: A connection attempt failed.

chrome.name: ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED
chrome.desc: The host name could not be resolved.

chrome.name: ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED
chrome.desc: The Internet connection has been lost.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR
chrome.desc: An SSL protocol error occurred.

chrome.name: ERR_ADDRESS_INVALID
chrome.desc: The IP address or port number is invalid (e.g., cannot connect to the IP address 0 or the port 0).

chrome.name: ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE
chrome.desc: The IP address is unreachable. This usually means that there is no route to the specified host or network.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_NEEDED
chrome.desc: The server requested a client certificate for SSL client authentication.

chrome.name: ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: A tunnel connection through the proxy could not be established. For more info see the comment on PROXY_UNABLE_TO_CONNECT_TO_DESTINATION.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH
chrome.desc: The client and server don't support a common SSL protocol version or cipher suite.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_RENEGOTIATION_REQUESTED
chrome.desc: The server requested a renegotiation (rehandshake).

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED
chrome.desc: The proxy requested authentication (for tunnel establishment) with an unsupported method.

chrome.name: ERR_BAD_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT
chrome.desc: The SSL handshake failed because of a bad or missing client certificate.

chrome.name: ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT
chrome.desc: A connection attempt timed out.

chrome.name: ERR_HOST_RESOLVER_QUEUE_TOO_LARGE
chrome.desc: There are too many pending DNS resolves, so a request in the queue was aborted.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKS_CONNECTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: Failed establishing a connection to the SOCKS proxy server for a target host.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKS_CONNECTION_HOST_UNREACHABLE
chrome.desc: The SOCKS proxy server failed establishing connection to the target host because that host is unreachable.

chrome.name: ERR_ALPN_NEGOTIATION_FAILED
chrome.desc: The request to negotiate an alternate protocol failed.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_NO_RENEGOTIATION
chrome.desc: The peer sent an SSL no_renegotiation alert message.

chrome.name: ERR_WINSOCK_UNEXPECTED_WRITTEN_BYTES
chrome.desc: Winsock sometimes reports more data written than passed. This is probably due to a broken LSP.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_DECOMPRESSION_FAILURE_ALERT
chrome.desc: An SSL peer sent us a fatal decompression_failure alert. This typically occurs when a peer selects DEFLATE compression in the mistaken belief that it supports it.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_BAD_RECORD_MAC_ALERT
chrome.desc: An SSL peer sent us a fatal bad_record_mac alert. This has been observed from servers with buggy DEFLATE support.

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_AUTH_REQUESTED
chrome.desc: The proxy requested authentication (for tunnel establishment).

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: Could not create a connection to the proxy server. An error occurred either in resolving its name, or in connecting a socket to it. Note that this does NOT include failures during the actual "CONNECT" method of an HTTP proxy.

chrome.name: ERR_MANDATORY_PROXY_CONFIGURATION_FAILED
chrome.desc: A mandatory proxy configuration could not be used. Currently this means that a mandatory PAC script could not be fetched, parsed or executed.

chrome.name: ERR_PRECONNECT_MAX_SOCKET_LIMIT
chrome.desc: We've hit the max socket limit for the socket pool while preconnecting. We don't bother trying to preconnect more sockets.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_ACCESS_DENIED
chrome.desc: The permission to use the SSL client certificate's private key was denied.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_NO_PRIVATE_KEY
chrome.desc: The SSL client certificate has no private key.

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_CERTIFICATE_INVALID
chrome.desc: The certificate presented by the HTTPS Proxy was invalid.

chrome.name: ERR_NAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: An error occurred when trying to do a name resolution (DNS).

chrome.name: ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED
chrome.desc: Permission to access the network was denied. This is used to distinguish errors that were most likely caused by a firewall from other access denied errors. See also ERR_ACCESS_DENIED.

chrome.name: ERR_TEMPORARILY_THROTTLED
chrome.desc: The request throttler module cancelled this request to avoid DDOS.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_SIGNATURE_FAILED
chrome.desc: We were unable to sign the CertificateVerify data of an SSL client auth handshake with the client certificate's private key.

chrome.name: ERR_MSG_TOO_BIG
chrome.desc: The message was too large for the transport. (for example a UDP message which exceeds size threshold).

chrome.name: ERR_WS_PROTOCOL_ERROR
chrome.desc: Websocket protocol error. Indicates that we are terminating the connection due to a malformed frame or other protocol violation.

chrome.name: ERR_ADDRESS_IN_USE
chrome.desc: Returned when attempting to bind an address that is already in use.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_PINNED_KEY_NOT_IN_CERT_CHAIN
chrome.desc: The certificate didn't match the built-in public key pins for the host name. The pins are set in net/http/transport_security_state.cc and require that one of a set of public keys exist on the path from the leaf to the root.

chrome.name: ERR_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED
chrome.desc: Server request for client certificate did not contain any types we support.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_DECRYPT_ERROR_ALERT
chrome.desc: An SSL peer sent us a fatal decrypt_error alert. This typically occurs when a peer could not correctly verify a signature (in CertificateVerify or ServerKeyExchange) or validate a Finished message.

chrome.name: ERR_WS_THROTTLE_QUEUE_TOO_LARGE
chrome.desc: There are too many pending WebSocketJob instances, so the new job was not pushed to the queue.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_SERVER_CERT_CHANGED
chrome.desc: The SSL server certificate changed in a renegotiation.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME_ALERT
chrome.desc: The SSL server sent us a fatal unrecognized_name alert.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_SET_RECEIVE_BUFFER_SIZE_ERROR
chrome.desc: Failed to set the socket's receive buffer size as requested.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_SET_SEND_BUFFER_SIZE_ERROR
chrome.desc: Failed to set the socket's send buffer size as requested.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_RECEIVE_BUFFER_SIZE_UNCHANGEABLE
chrome.desc: Failed to set the socket's receive buffer size as requested, despite success return code from setsockopt.

chrome.name: ERR_SOCKET_SEND_BUFFER_SIZE_UNCHANGEABLE
chrome.desc: Failed to set the socket's send buffer size as requested, despite success return code from setsockopt.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_BAD_FORMAT
chrome.desc: Failed to import a client certificate from the platform store into the SSL library.

chrome.name: ERR_ICANN_NAME_COLLISION
chrome.desc: Resolving a hostname to an IP address list included the IPv4 address "127.0.53.53". This is a special IP address which ICANN has recommended to indicate there was a name collision, and alert admins to a potential problem.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_SERVER_CERT_BAD_FORMAT
chrome.desc: The SSL server presented a certificate which could not be decoded. This is not a certificate error code as no X509Certificate object is available. This error is fatal.

chrome.name: ERR_CT_STH_PARSING_FAILED
chrome.desc: Certificate Transparency: Received a signed tree head that failed to parse.

chrome.name: ERR_CT_STH_INCOMPLETE
chrome.desc: Certificate Transparency: Received a signed tree head whose JSON parsing was OK but was missing some of the fields.

chrome.name: ERR_UNABLE_TO_REUSE_CONNECTION_FOR_PROXY_AUTH
chrome.desc: The attempt to reuse a connection to send proxy auth credentials failed before the AuthController was used to generate credentials. The caller should reuse the controller with a new connection. This error is only used internally by the network stack.

chrome.name: ERR_CT_CONSISTENCY_PROOF_PARSING_FAILED
chrome.desc: Certificate Transparency: Failed to parse the received consistency proof.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_OBSOLETE_CIPHER
chrome.desc: The SSL server required an unsupported cipher suite that has since been removed. This error will temporarily be signaled on a fallback for one or two releases immediately following a cipher suite's removal, after which the fallback will be removed.

chrome.name: ERR_WS_UPGRADE
chrome.desc: When a WebSocket handshake is done successfully and the connection has been upgraded, the URLRequest is cancelled with this error code.

chrome.name: ERR_READ_IF_READY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
chrome.desc: Socket ReadIfReady support is not implemented. This error should not be user visible, because the normal Read() method is used as a fallback.

chrome.name: ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE
chrome.desc: No socket buffer space is available.

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_NO_COMMON_ALGORITHMS
chrome.desc: There were no common signature algorithms between our client certificate private key and the server's preferences.

chrome.name: ERR_EARLY_DATA_REJECTED
chrome.desc: TLS 1.3 early data was rejected by the server. This will be received before any data is returned from the socket. The request should be retried with early data disabled.

chrome.name: ERR_WRONG_VERSION_ON_EARLY_DATA
chrome.desc: TLS 1.3 early data was offered, but the server responded with TLS 1.2 or earlier. This is an internal error code to account for a backwards-compatibility issue with early data and TLS 1.2. It will be received before any data is returned from the socket. The request should be retried with early data disabled.

chrome.name: ERR_TLS13_DOWNGRADE_DETECTED
chrome.desc: TLS 1.3 was enabled, but a lower version was negotiated and the server returned a value indicating it supported TLS 1.3. This is part of a security check in TLS 1.3, but it may also indicate the user is behind a buggy TLS-terminating proxy which implemented TLS 1.2 incorrectly. (See https://crbug.com/boringssl/226.)

chrome.name: ERR_SSL_KEY_USAGE_INCOMPATIBLE
chrome.desc: The server's certificate has a keyUsage extension incompatible with the negotiated TLS key exchange method.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_ECH_CONFIG_LIST
chrome.desc: The ECHConfigList fetched over DNS cannot be parsed.

chrome.name: ERR_ECH_NOT_NEGOTIATED
chrome.desc: ECH was enabled, but the server was unable to decrypt the encrypted ClientHello.

chrome.name: ERR_ECH_FALLBACK_CERTIFICATE_INVALID
chrome.desc: ECH was enabled, the server was unable to decrypt the encrypted ClientHello, and additionally did not present a certificate valid for the public name.

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_UNABLE_TO_CONNECT_TO_DESTINATION
chrome.desc: An attempt to proxy a request failed because the proxy wasn't able to successfully connect to the destination. This likely indicates an issue with the request itself (for instance, the hostname failed to resolve to an IP address or the destination server refused the connection). This error code is used to indicate that the error is outside the control of the proxy server and thus the proxy chain should not be marked as bad. This is in contrast to ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED which is used for general purpose errors connecting to the proxy and by the proxy request response handling when a proxy delegate doesn't indicate via a different error code whether the failure was specific to the destination. By default, neither error code causes the proxy chain to be marked as bad, though a ProxyDelegate may override fallback behavior via CanFalloverToNextProxyOverride().

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_DELEGATE_CANCELED_CONNECT_REQUEST
chrome.desc: Some implementations of ProxyDelegate query a separate entity to know whether it should cancel tunnel prior to: - The HTTP CONNECT requests being sent out - The HTTP CONNECT response being parsed by //net An example is CronetProxyDelegate: Cronet allows developers to decide whether the tunnel being established should be canceled.

chrome.name: ERR_CONTROL_MSG_TOO_BIG
chrome.desc: The control message was too large for the transport. (for example a UDP message control data exceeds size threshold).

chrome.name: ERR_MULTICAST_NOT_ALLOWED
chrome.desc: Direct Sockets attempted to connect to or send a packet to a multicast address without 'direct-sockets-multicast' permissions policy.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate whose common name did not match the host name. This could mean:

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that, by our clock, appears to either not yet be valid or to have expired. This could mean:

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that is signed by an authority we don't trust. The could mean:

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_CONTAINS_ERRORS
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that contains errors. This error is not recoverable.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_NO_REVOCATION_MECHANISM
chrome.desc: The certificate has no mechanism for determining if it is revoked. In effect, this certificate cannot be revoked.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_UNABLE_TO_CHECK_REVOCATION
chrome.desc: Revocation information for the security certificate for this site is not available. This could mean:

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_REVOKED
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate has been revoked. We have the capability to ignore this error, but it is probably not the thing to do.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_INVALID
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that is invalid. This error is not recoverable.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_WEAK_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that is signed using a weak signature algorithm.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_NON_UNIQUE_NAME
chrome.desc: The host name specified in the certificate is not unique.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_WEAK_KEY
chrome.desc: The server responded with a certificate that contains a weak key (e.g. a too-small RSA key).

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_NAME_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION
chrome.desc: The certificate claimed DNS names that are in violation of name constraints.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_VALIDITY_TOO_LONG
chrome.desc: The certificate's validity period is too long.

chrome.name: ERR_CERTIFICATE_TRANSPARENCY_REQUIRED
chrome.desc: Certificate Transparency was required for this connection, but the server did not provide CT information that complied with the policy.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_KNOWN_INTERCEPTION_BLOCKED
chrome.desc: The certificate is known to be used for interception by an entity other the device owner.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_SELF_SIGNED_LOCAL_NETWORK
chrome.desc: The certificate is self signed and it's being used for either an RFC1918 IP literal URL, or a url ending in .local.

chrome.name: ERR_CERT_END
chrome.desc: The value immediately past the last certificate error code.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_URL
chrome.desc: The URL is invalid.

chrome.name: ERR_DISALLOWED_URL_SCHEME
chrome.desc: The scheme of the URL is disallowed.

chrome.name: ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME
chrome.desc: The scheme of the URL is unknown.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_REDIRECT
chrome.desc: Attempting to load an URL resulted in a redirect to an invalid URL.

chrome.name: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS
chrome.desc: Attempting to load an URL resulted in too many redirects.

chrome.name: ERR_UNSAFE_REDIRECT
chrome.desc: Attempting to load an URL resulted in an unsafe redirect (e.g., a redirect to file:// is considered unsafe).

chrome.name: ERR_UNSAFE_PORT
chrome.desc: Attempting to load an URL with an unsafe port number. These are port numbers that correspond to services, which are not robust to spurious input that may be constructed as a result of an allowed web construct (e.g., HTTP looks a lot like SMTP, so form submission to port 25 is denied).

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE
chrome.desc: The server's response was invalid.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_CHUNKED_ENCODING
chrome.desc: Error in chunked transfer encoding.

chrome.name: ERR_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
chrome.desc: The server did not support the request method.

chrome.name: ERR_UNEXPECTED_PROXY_AUTH
chrome.desc: The response was 407 (Proxy Authentication Required), yet we did not send the request to a proxy.

chrome.name: ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE
chrome.desc: The server closed the connection without sending any data.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_TOO_BIG
chrome.desc: The headers section of the response is too large.

chrome.name: ERR_PAC_SCRIPT_FAILED
chrome.desc: The evaluation of the PAC script failed.

chrome.name: ERR_REQUEST_RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE
chrome.desc: The response was 416 (Requested range not satisfiable) and the server cannot satisfy the range requested.

chrome.name: ERR_MALFORMED_IDENTITY
chrome.desc: The identity used for authentication is invalid.

chrome.name: ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED
chrome.desc: Content decoding of the response body failed.

chrome.name: ERR_NETWORK_IO_SUSPENDED
chrome.desc: An operation could not be completed because all network IO is suspended.

chrome.name: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES
chrome.desc: There are no supported proxies in the provided list.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR
chrome.desc: There is an HTTP/2 protocol error.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS
chrome.desc: Credentials could not be established during HTTP Authentication.

chrome.name: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_AUTH_SCHEME
chrome.desc: An HTTP Authentication scheme was tried which is not supported on this machine.

chrome.name: ERR_ENCODING_DETECTION_FAILED
chrome.desc: Detecting the encoding of the response failed.

chrome.name: ERR_MISSING_AUTH_CREDENTIALS
chrome.desc: (GSSAPI) No Kerberos credentials were available during HTTP Authentication.

chrome.name: ERR_UNEXPECTED_SECURITY_LIBRARY_STATUS
chrome.desc: An unexpected, but documented, SSPI or GSSAPI status code was returned.

chrome.name: ERR_MISCONFIGURED_AUTH_ENVIRONMENT
chrome.desc: The environment was not set up correctly for authentication (for example, no KDC could be found or the principal is unknown.

chrome.name: ERR_UNDOCUMENTED_SECURITY_LIBRARY_STATUS
chrome.desc: An undocumented SSPI or GSSAPI status code was returned.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_BODY_TOO_BIG_TO_DRAIN
chrome.desc: The HTTP response was too big to drain.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_MULTIPLE_CONTENT_LENGTH
chrome.desc: The HTTP response contained multiple distinct Content-Length headers.

chrome.name: ERR_INCOMPLETE_HTTP2_HEADERS
chrome.desc: HTTP/2 headers have been received, but not all of them - status or version headers are missing, so we're expecting additional frames to complete them.

chrome.name: ERR_PAC_NOT_IN_DHCP
chrome.desc: No PAC URL configuration could be retrieved from DHCP. This can indicate either a failure to retrieve the DHCP configuration, or that there was no PAC URL configured in DHCP.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_MULTIPLE_CONTENT_DISPOSITION
chrome.desc: The HTTP response contained multiple Content-Disposition headers.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_MULTIPLE_LOCATION
chrome.desc: The HTTP response contained multiple Location headers.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM
chrome.desc: HTTP/2 server refused the request without processing, and sent either a GOAWAY frame with error code NO_ERROR and Last-Stream-ID lower than the stream id corresponding to the request indicating that this request has not been processed yet, or a RST_STREAM frame with error code REFUSED_STREAM. Client MAY retry (on a different connection). See RFC7540 Section 8.1.4.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_PING_FAILED
chrome.desc: HTTP/2 server didn't respond to the PING message.

chrome.name: ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH
chrome.desc: The HTTP response body transferred fewer bytes than were advertised by the Content-Length header when the connection is closed.

chrome.name: ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING
chrome.desc: The HTTP response body is transferred with Chunked-Encoding, but the terminating zero-length chunk was never sent when the connection is closed.

chrome.name: ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR
chrome.desc: There is a QUIC protocol error.

chrome.name: ERR_RESPONSE_HEADERS_TRUNCATED
chrome.desc: The HTTP headers were truncated by an EOF.

chrome.name: ERR_QUIC_HANDSHAKE_FAILED
chrome.desc: The QUIC crypto handshake failed. This means that the server was unable to read any requests sent, so they may be resent.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_INADEQUATE_TRANSPORT_SECURITY
chrome.desc: Transport security is inadequate for the HTTP/2 version.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR
chrome.desc: The peer violated HTTP/2 flow control.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR
chrome.desc: The peer sent an improperly sized HTTP/2 frame.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_COMPRESSION_ERROR
chrome.desc: Decoding or encoding of compressed HTTP/2 headers failed.

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_AUTH_REQUESTED_WITH_NO_CONNECTION
chrome.desc: Proxy Auth Requested without a valid Client Socket Handle.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED
chrome.desc: HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED error code received on HTTP/2 session.

chrome.name: ERR_PROXY_HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED
chrome.desc: HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED error code received on HTTP/2 session to proxy.

chrome.name: ERR_PAC_SCRIPT_TERMINATED
chrome.desc: The PAC script terminated fatally and must be reloaded.

chrome.name: ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE
chrome.desc: The server was expected to return an HTTP/1.x response, but did not. Rather than treat it as HTTP/0.9, this error is returned.

chrome.name: ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_INIT_FAILED
chrome.desc: Initializing content decoding failed.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_RST_STREAM_NO_ERROR_RECEIVED
chrome.desc: Received HTTP/2 RST_STREAM frame with NO_ERROR error code. This error should be handled internally by HTTP/2 code, and should not make it above the SpdyStream layer.

chrome.name: ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES
chrome.desc: An HTTP transaction was retried too many times due for authentication or invalid certificates. This may be due to a bug in the net stack that would otherwise infinite loop, or if the server or proxy continually requests fresh credentials or presents a fresh invalid certificate.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_CLOSED
chrome.desc: Received an HTTP/2 frame on a closed stream.

chrome.name: ERR_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_FAILURE
chrome.desc: The server returned a non-2xx HTTP response code.

chrome.name: ERR_QUIC_CERT_ROOT_NOT_KNOWN
chrome.desc: The certificate presented on a QUIC connection does not chain to a known root and the origin connected to is not on a list of domains where unknown roots are allowed.

chrome.name: ERR_QUIC_GOAWAY_REQUEST_CAN_BE_RETRIED
chrome.desc: A GOAWAY frame has been received indicating that the request has not been processed and is therefore safe to retry on a different connection.

chrome.name: ERR_TOO_MANY_ACCEPT_CH_RESTARTS
chrome.desc: The ACCEPT_CH restart has been triggered too many times

chrome.name: ERR_INCONSISTENT_IP_ADDRESS_SPACE
chrome.desc: The IP address space of the remote endpoint differed from the previous observed value during the same request. Any cache entry for the affected request should be invalidated.

chrome.name: ERR_CACHED_IP_ADDRESS_SPACE_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_POLICY

ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED.meaning: The name lookup (DNS) failed, so no connection to the website was even attempted. Either the address is misspelled or no longer exists, or the DNS server your network uses gave no usable answer. If other sites open, check the spelling first, then test the DNS server.

ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED.meaning: Chrome sees no network connection on this device. The website, your provider and the internet at large were never asked – the cause sits between this device and the router.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT.meaning: The name was found, a connection was tried and nobody answered in time. DNS is not the problem. Either the server is down or overloaded, or something on the way silently drops the traffic – a firewall, a VPN or a filter. The comparison with mobile data separates the two.

ERR_TIMED_OUT.meaning: An operation ran out of time without an answer. For a web page that means the same as a connection timeout: the server or the path to it did not respond. Compare with mobile data to see which side it follows.

ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.meaning: Something at that address answered and actively refused the connection. That is different from a timeout: the path works. It fits a server whose web service is not running, an address with a wrong port, or a firewall that rejects instead of ignoring.

ERR_CONNECTION_RESET.meaning: A connection existed and was cut off. The cut can come from the server or from anything in between that inspects traffic – security software, a company or hotel filter, a VPN. If the site opens on mobile data, look at your own network and device.

ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED.meaning: The other side closed the connection before sending a page. As with a reset, the server or a device in between ended it; compare with another network and another browser.

ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED.meaning: The connection was given up because the other side did not confirm data in time. It points to an unstable path – weak Wi-Fi, a struggling router or a server in trouble – rather than to a wrong setting.

ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED.meaning: The connection attempt failed without a more specific reason. On its own it does not name a layer; the comparison checks (other sites, mobile data, another browser) have to.

ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE.meaning: The device knows the server’s address but has no route to it. That is a network-level fault: the router, the provider or a VPN – not the browser and usually not the website.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED.meaning: The device’s network changed while the page was loading – a switch between Wi-Fi, cable and mobile data, a VPN connecting, or a new address from the router. Reload once. If it keeps coming back, the Wi-Fi link or the VPN is unstable.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT.meaning: Something inside the browser blocked the request – in practice an extension such as a content blocker. The network and the website are not involved. A private window, where extensions are normally off, shows it at once.

ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR.meaning: A policy set by whoever manages this browser or device blocks the address. On a work or school device that is IT’s decision; on a private device, check whether the browser says it is “managed” and by whom.

ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED.meaning: The browser was not allowed to use the network. Chromium’s own note says this is most likely a firewall – look at the firewall or security software on this device, not at the router.

ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED.meaning: The browser is set to use a proxy server and could not reach it. The website never saw the request. Check the proxy setting of the system or of a VPN or security app that installed one.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED.meaning: A connection through a proxy could not be set up. As with other proxy errors, the place to look is the proxy or VPN configured on this device or network.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.meaning: The site sent the browser from address to address in a circle. Either the website is misconfigured or a cookie it stored in your browser no longer fits. A private window tells the two apart.

ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE.meaning: The server accepted the connection and closed it without sending anything. That is the server’s or an in-between filter’s doing, not a setting in your browser.

ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR.meaning: Browser and server could not set up the encrypted connection. Do not look for a way round it. Test another device and another network to see whether it follows the website or your side – security software that inspects encrypted traffic can cause it.

ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH.meaning: Browser and server have no encryption method in common. That is decided by the server’s configuration or by software that inspects encrypted traffic; nothing on a normal home device needs changing.

ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID.meaning: By your device’s clock the site’s certificate is expired or not yet valid. Chromium lists three possible reasons: an attacker with an old certificate, a misconfigured server – or a wrong clock on your device. Check date, time and time zone first; do not click through.

ERR_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_FAILURE.meaning: The server answered, but with an HTTP error status. The connection and DNS are fine; the status code (404, 500, 503 …) says more.

ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR.meaning: An error inside the HTTP/2 conversation with the server. Usually the website’s side or a device in between; test another network and another browser before changing anything.

ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR.meaning: An error in QUIC, the transport Chrome uses for HTTP/3. Usually the website’s side or a network that handles QUIC badly; test another network and another browser.

ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND.meaning: A file on this device was not found – as with an address that starts with file://. No network layer is involved.

ERR_INVALID_URL.meaning: The address itself is not a valid URL. Check for a typing mistake, a stray space or a missing part.

ERR_UNSAFE_PORT.meaning: The address contains a port number that Chrome refuses to connect to for web pages. That is the browser’s own safety rule, not a network fault.

ERR_DNS_TIMED_OUT.meaning: The DNS server did not answer in time. The website was never contacted; the fault is between this device and the DNS server – router, provider or a DNS setting on the device.

ERR_DNS_SERVER_FAILURE.meaning: The DNS server answered with a failure. The website was never contacted; test another DNS server to see whether your network’s DNS is the problem.

System.meaning: A general or local error – files, memory, permissions or a cancelled request. On its own it does not point to the router, the provider or the website.

Connection.meaning: The connection to the server or to a proxy failed at network or encryption level. Compare with another website and with mobile data to see whether it follows the website or your network.

Certificate.meaning: A certificate error: the browser could not confirm that the site is the one it claims to be. Do not click through and do not type passwords or card numbers. Check the date and time on your device, then try the site later or from another network; if the warning stays, only the website’s owner can fix it.

HTTP.meaning: A problem in the HTTP exchange with the server – the connection itself worked. Most of these can only be fixed by the website; a private window shows whether your browser data plays a part.

Cache.meaning: Concerns Chrome’s local cache of earlier downloads, not the network.

DNS resolver.meaning: The name lookup failed. The website was never contacted; the fault is on the way to the DNS server or at the DNS server.

Certificate manager.meaning: Concerns importing or managing certificates in the browser, not loading a normal web page.

Blob.meaning: Concerns data the page handles inside the browser, not the network.

Unnamed range.meaning: Chromium’s list gives this range no name.

DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN.meaning: Chrome ran its own DNS test: the DNS servers work, so the name does not exist. Check the spelling of the address. If it is right, the site’s domain may have lapsed – or a filter on your network answers “no such name” on purpose.

DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET.meaning: Chrome’s DNS test found no internet connection at all. Start with the connection, not with the website.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_BAD_CONFIG.meaning: Chrome’s DNS test says the DNS settings are wrong or the DNS servers are down. Look for a manual DNS entry or a VPN on this device, then at the router.

DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_BAD_SECURE_CONFIG.meaning: Chrome’s DNS test failed with the secure DNS (DNS over HTTPS) provider set in Chrome. The network’s normal DNS may be fine – check Chrome’s secure DNS setting.

DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_INCONCLUSIVE.meaning: Chrome’s DNS test reached no conclusion. Use the comparison checks instead.

DNS_PROBE_STARTED.meaning: Chrome is still testing DNS; the code on the page changes when the test has finished. Wait a few seconds.

DNS_PROBE_POSSIBLE.meaning: Chrome has not run its DNS test yet; the code on the page changes when it has.

DNS_PROBE_NOT_RUN.meaning: Chrome did not run its DNS test, so the code says nothing about the cause.

301.meaning: The address has moved permanently; browsers follow it automatically. You only see it in tools, not as an error.

302.meaning: A temporary redirect; browsers follow it automatically. Seen as an “error” only when redirects loop.

304.meaning: Not an error: the server says your stored copy is still current.

400.meaning: The server rejected the request as malformed. From a browser, data stored for that site (cookies) can be the cause: test a private window, then clear that one site’s data.

401.meaning: The server wants a valid sign-in for this address. Sign in again; if the page belongs to a company or school, the account needs access.

403.meaning: The server understood the request and refuses it. Your connection works. The site decides this – by account, by country or network, or by the address you come from, for example when you use a VPN.

404.meaning: The server is up but has nothing at this exact address. Check the spelling after the domain name; an old link or bookmark is the usual reason. Nothing on your device needs fixing.

408.meaning: The server gave up waiting for the browser’s request. Reload once; if it repeats on a slow or unstable connection, look at the Wi-Fi link.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

410.meaning: The page was removed on purpose and is not coming back at this address.

429.meaning: Too many requests from your address or account in a short time. Wait – every reload adds another request. On a shared network or VPN, the limit is shared with others.

451.meaning: The site withholds the page for legal reasons, typically depending on the country you connect from. Nothing is broken on your side.

500.meaning: The website’s server ran into an error of its own. Only the site can fix it; try again later or check its status page.

502.meaning: A server in front of the website (gateway or proxy) got an invalid answer from the server behind it. A problem inside the website’s infrastructure – wait and retry.

503.meaning: The server is temporarily overloaded or down for maintenance. Wait and retry; a status page often confirms it.

504.meaning: A gateway in front of the website waited too long for the server behind it. As with 502, the website’s side.

1.meaning: Informational: an interim answer while the request continues. Not an error.

2.meaning: Successful: the server did what was asked. If the page still looks wrong, the cause is in the page or the browser, not in the transfer.

3.meaning: Redirection: the browser is sent to another address and normally follows without showing anything.

4.meaning: Client error class: the server answered and says the request cannot be fulfilled as sent. Your connection, DNS and the server all work; check the address, your sign-in and the site’s data in your browser.

5.meaning: Server error class: the server answered and says it failed. Your device and network work; only the website can fix it.

169.254.0.0/16.meaning: A link-local address: the device gave it to itself because no DHCP server – normally your router – answered. With such an address the device can reach neither the router nor the internet. The fault is in the link between this device and the router, not at the provider or the website.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

Private-Use.meaning: A private address, as a home or office router hands out. It shows that the device is joined to the network and received an address, so the device–router link works at this level. Private addresses are not visible from the internet; many devices worldwide use the same ones.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

100.64.0.0/10.meaning: Shared address space, reserved for the link between a customer’s router and the provider when the provider uses carrier-grade NAT. If your router shows such an address as its internet (WAN) address, you share a public address with other customers: browsing works, but port forwarding from the internet to your home cannot.

127.0.0.0/8.meaning: A loopback address: it always means “this device itself”. A page or tool using it talks to software on the same computer, never to the network.

0.0.0.0/8.meaning: An address a device uses for itself before it has a real one. Shown as the device’s address, it means no address has been assigned yet.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

0.0.0.0/32.meaning: The placeholder for “this host” before an address is assigned. Shown as the device’s address, it means it has none yet.

next.label: Diagnosis: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

255.255.255.255/32.meaning: The limited broadcast address: “everyone on this local network”. Never the address of a single device.

224.0.0.0/4.meaning: A multicast address: used to reach a group of devices at once, for example when devices look for printers on the local network. Never the address of a single device.

ff00::/8.meaning: An IPv6 multicast address: used to reach a group of devices at once. Never the address of a single device.

fe80::/10.meaning: An IPv6 link-local address. Every IPv6 device has one and it only works inside the local network, so it is normal to see it next to other addresses. If it is the only IPv6 address, the network offers no IPv6 internet access – IPv4 may still work.

fc00::/7.meaning: An IPv6 unique local address: the IPv6 counterpart of a private address. It works inside your network and is not reachable from the internet.

::1/128.meaning: The IPv6 loopback address: “this device itself”.

::/128.meaning: The unspecified IPv6 address: a device without an address yet.

Documentation.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

publicV4.meaning: A public IPv4 address. Behind a home router a device normally shows a private address instead; a public one means the device is connected directly to the modem or to the provider’s network, without a router in between. As the router’s internet (WAN) address it is the normal case.

publicV6.meaning: A public (global) IPv6 address. Unlike IPv4, it is normal for every device at home to have one: IPv6 does not need private addresses and address translation.

192.0.2.0/24.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

198.51.100.0/24.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

203.0.113.0/24.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

2001:db8::/32.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

3fff::/20.meaning: A range reserved for examples in manuals and documentation. A real device should never have it – if you copied it from instructions, replace it with your own value.

wu.listed: Microsoft’s list names the error and the Windows Update component that reported it. It is written for IT administrators and gives no fix; the name still narrows it down – “PT” codes come from talking to the update server, “DM” from downloading, “UH” from installing, “DS” from the local update database.
wu.common: Microsoft’s troubleshooting article covers this code with a cause and a mitigation written for administrators. Read the mitigation there; for a home PC, start with the safe steps in our guide before using any command.
wu.missing: This code is not in Microsoft’s two lists as retrieved (Windows Update error codes by component; Common Windows Update errors). Many 0x8007… codes are general Windows errors passed through by Windows Update. Search the exact code on Microsoft’s own support site only.
